The cart repeatedly hit its rear-left corner at the bend; pulling forward and retrying from nearly the same position did not create clearance, and eventually put the mower's front-right corner into the rail. Inspect both sides before moving and reposition early toward the right-hand opening. This short cart reacts quickly, so use small steering corrections and watch its rear corners, not just the hitch angle.
--- round 1, driver 2:
A straight reverse hit the left rail at the first bend; starting the rightward arc earlier cleared that section. Straightening too early then put the cart's rear-right corner into the rail repeatedly. Watch both cart corners and the vehicle front, and use the visible rails to judge the bend rather than relying on distance alone. The short cart reacts quickly, so make small corrections at low speed and allow room to pull forward before getting trapped.
--- round 1, driver 3:
The cart’s rear-left corner touched the rail when I tried to follow the apparent centre of the nearby rails. Pulling forward released it and straightened the hitch. A slow rightward cart turn through the bend worked, followed by gradual straightening for the bay. Prioritise rear-corner clearance and begin following the cart early: this short trailer reacts quickly and can fold fast.
--- end of notes
